I see, Bethany. I’ll run some quick diagnostics on CPU and memory usage and then guide you through a few optimization steps.
I’ve adjusted your Docker resource recommendations and sent you step-by-step instructions. Please follow them and let me know if performance improves.
That worked! Everything feels much faster now, thanks.

events.message: Collected system info: CPU at 98% and memory at 90% when Docker is running.
Diagnosis: resource contention due to Docker and multiple heavy apps (linked to KB-003).
Solution: reduce Docker CPU/RAM allocation and disable non-essential startup apps.
Ticket automatically resolved after user confirmed performance is normal.

conversation.message: Hi Amy, I’m your IT support assistant. I see you’re having trouble with VPN access. Let’s fix that.

knowledge_base.title: VPN authentication fails after password reset
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: VPN authentication failed; password works for email; MFA prompt not showing or failing
knowledge_base.summary: Typical VPN failures after a password change are caused by cached credentials or outdated VPN profiles on the client.
resolution_steps: Ask user to close the VPN client completely, including any system tray icons.
Open Windows Credential Manager and remove all entries related to the VPN gateway and corporate domain.
Sign out of all Microsoft 365 desktop apps and sign back in using the new domain password.
Delete the existing VPN profile in the VPN client.
Import the latest VPN configuration file from the official IT portal.
Trigger MFA re-registration if MFA prompts are failing or not appearing.
Reconnect to VPN and verify access to internal services such as Jira, Git, and Confluence.
If the issue persists, capture logs and screenshots and escalate to the network team.

knowledge_base.title: Outlook not syncing after mailbox migration to cloud
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Outlook stuck on 'Updating inbox' or 'Trying to connect'; emails visible in webmail but not in desktop app
knowledge_base.summary: Post-migration Outlook sync issues are usually due to old profiles or corrupted OST files pointing to the legacy mailbox.
resolution_steps: Confirm the user can access email successfully via Outlook on the web.
In Outlook desktop, open Account Settings and remove the old Exchange/Office 365 profile.
Open Control Panel → Mail → Show Profiles and delete outdated profiles that reference on-prem servers.
Create a new mail profile and add the user’s account via AutoDiscover.
Enable 'Use Cached Exchange Mode' with a 1–2 year sync window.
Allow Outlook to rebuild the OST file completely before closing the app.
If OST corruption is suspected, run the built-in repair tool or recreate the OST file from scratch.
If several users in the same department see similar symptoms, create a problem record for the messaging team.

knowledge_base.title: Developer laptop slow when running Docker and IDEs
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: High CPU and memory usage when Docker, Chrome, and IDE are running simultaneously on standard developer image
knowledge_base.summary: On standard 16 GB RAM developer laptops, Docker plus heavy IDEs and browsers can starve system resources unless Docker is tuned and startup apps are trimmed.
resolution_steps: Open Task Manager and confirm CPU and RAM usage when Docker workloads are running.
In Docker Desktop → Settings → Resources, reduce vCPU and RAM allocation (e.g., to 4 vCPUs and 4 GB RAM on a 16 GB machine).
Stop and disable unnecessary containers and images that start automatically.
Open the Startup tab in Task Manager and disable non-essential applications (Teams auto-start, chat clients, screen recorders, etc.).
Run the Company Software Center and install the latest graphics and chipset drivers available for the device.
Reboot the laptop and verify that VS Code, the browser, and Docker remain responsive under normal workloads.
If performance is still poor, evaluate hardware upgrade (RAM/SSD) or move heavy builds to remote build agents.

knowledge_base.title: Handling repeated BSODs on critical user laptops
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Blue screen errors multiple times per day, recurring across tickets, especially for client-facing staff
knowledge_base.summary: Multiple BSOD incidents within a short period usually indicate failing hardware (SSD/RAM) or critical driver conflicts and should trigger hardware replacement for critical staff.
resolution_steps: Review incident history: if there are two or more BSOD tickets within 7 days for the same device, classify as potential hardware failure.
Collect minidump files and run quick diagnostics on memory and disk (SMART tests).
Mark the user as 'critical' if they are client-facing or manage production systems.
Create a hardware replacement task and arrange a loaner or replacement laptop the same day whenever possible.
Back up the user profile to OneDrive/SharePoint and verify that key project folders are fully synced.
Issue a new device with the standard corporate image and restore required applications from Software Center.
Schedule a short session to test conferencing apps (Zoom/Teams) and development tools with the user.
Monitor for 48 hours; if no further BSODs occur, close the root cause as 'hardware replaced'.
Document asset tags, serial numbers, diagnostic results, and replacement device details in the ticket.

knowledge_base.title: USB peripherals not working through docking station
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Mouse/keyboard intermittently disconnects when plugged into dock but works fine directly on laptop
knowledge_base.summary: Intermittent USB peripheral issues through a dock are commonly due to outdated dock firmware, power problems, or a failing USB hub on the dock.
resolution_steps: Test the mouse/keyboard directly on the laptop to confirm the device itself is healthy.
Update docking station firmware and drivers from the vendor’s official support site.
Check that the dock’s power adapter has the correct wattage and is firmly plugged in.
Move the device to a different USB port on the dock, preferring back-panel ports for stability.
Disable USB selective suspend in Windows power options for heavily used docking stations.
If issues persist, swap the dock with a known-good unit and re-test the peripherals.
If multiple users with the same dock model report similar problems, raise a problem ticket with hardware engineering and procurement.

knowledge_base.title: Slow boot after Windows update
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Laptop takes more than 5–10 minutes to boot after a major Windows feature update
knowledge_base.summary: Slow boot issues after large Windows updates are typically due to disk fragmentation, startup overload, or problematic drivers/services.
resolution_steps: Check boot time in Event Viewer (Diagnostics-Performance logs) to confirm excessive startup duration.
Run a disk health check and SMART test to rule out failing drives.
Open Task Manager → Startup tab and disable non-essential startup apps.
Run 'sfc /scannow' and 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' from an elevated Command Prompt.
Check Windows Update history and ensure all post-feature-update patches and driver updates are installed.
Update storage and chipset drivers from the device manufacturer or via Company Software Center.
Reboot and measure boot time again; if still slow, enable boot logging and analyze which drivers/services delay startup.
If the drive is close to capacity or shows high latency, consider SSD replacement for persistent cases.

knowledge_base.title: C: drive almost full on Windows laptop
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Low disk space warning; cannot save files; Windows slow; C: drive red in File Explorer
knowledge_base.summary: Most low-disk cases on the standard image are temporary files, Windows Update leftovers and a full Recycle Bin rather than genuine user data growth.
resolution_steps: Run a disk space check and record free space in GB before any change.
Clear the user and Windows temporary file folders.
Empty the Recycle Bin after confirming with the user that nothing is needed.
Run Windows Disk Cleanup including Windows Update cleanup.
Re-check free space and confirm at least 10 GB is now available.
If free space is still below 10 GB, review the Downloads folder and OneDrive sync settings with the user.
If the drive fills again within a week, escalate for disk upgrade assessment.

knowledge_base.title: Chrome using excessive memory and slowing the machine
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Chrome high RAM usage; machine slow with many tabs; fans loud; other apps unresponsive
knowledge_base.summary: Chrome holds a separate process per tab and extension. Large tab counts and unused extensions are the usual cause before any hardware fault.
resolution_steps: List the top processes by memory and confirm Chrome is the largest consumer.
Ask the user to save any work in open tabs before anything is closed.
Close inactive browser tabs, keeping the tab the user is working in.
Review installed extensions and disable any not required for work.
Clear the browser cache if the profile is large or slow to load.
If a single Chrome process is still consuming excessive memory, end that process with the user's approval.
Re-check memory usage and confirm the machine is responsive again.

knowledge_base.title: Internet connection keeps dropping on corporate laptop
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Intermittent disconnects; Wi-Fi drops then reconnects; pages time out; VPN drops repeatedly
knowledge_base.summary: Intermittent drops are usually a stale DHCP lease, a corrupted Winsock catalogue or a driver issue. Work from least disruptive to most.
resolution_steps: Test connectivity to an internal and an external host and record which fail.
Flush the DNS resolver cache and retest.
Release and renew the IP address, warning the user that the connection drops briefly.
Check the wireless adapter driver version and update it from the Company Software Center.
If drops continue, reset the Winsock catalogue. This requires a restart and IT-expert approval.
Reboot and verify that the connection stays up for at least 30 minutes of normal use.
If the issue persists after reset, capture logs and escalate to the network team.

knowledge_base.title: Internal sites unreachable but public internet works
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Cannot reach intranet, Jira or Confluence; public websites load; DNS errors; server not found on internal names
knowledge_base.summary: Internal-only failures usually point to stale DNS entries or a VPN split-tunnel misconfiguration rather than a broken connection.
resolution_steps: Confirm public internet works and note which internal hostnames fail.
Flush the DNS resolver cache.
Confirm the VPN client is connected and shows the corporate profile.
Test connectivity to an internal host by name and then by IP address.
If the IP works but the name does not, the issue is DNS. Confirm the correct DNS servers are assigned.
Disconnect and reconnect the VPN to reapply routes.
If internal names still fail, escalate to the network team with the test results.

knowledge_base.title: Print jobs stuck in queue and nothing prints
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Documents stay in print queue; printer shows offline; jobs will not delete; printing silently fails
knowledge_base.summary: A stalled Print Spooler service holds every queued job. Restarting the service clears it without touching the printer hardware.
resolution_steps: Confirm the printer is powered on, has paper and shows no hardware error.
Check whether other users can print to the same device, to separate device faults from client faults.
Restart the Print Spooler service. This briefly interrupts printing for the user and needs approval.
Clear any remaining stuck jobs from the queue.
Send a test page and confirm it prints.
If the test page fails, remove and re-add the printer from the print server.
If the device is faulty rather than the queue, raise a hardware ticket with the vendor.

knowledge_base.title: Laptop very slow to start up and log in
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Long boot time; desktop takes minutes to be usable; many apps open at login; spinning cursor after sign-in
knowledge_base.summary: Slow logins on the standard image are almost always caused by the number of applications configured to start automatically.
resolution_steps: Record the current startup time as reported by Task Manager.
List the programs configured to run at startup with their measured impact.
Identify non-essential items such as chat clients, update helpers and screen recorders.
Disable the non-essential startup items after confirming each one with the user.
Check for pending Windows updates and install them during the next maintenance window.
Reboot and confirm the machine reaches a usable desktop noticeably faster.
If boot time is still poor, check disk health before considering a hardware upgrade.

knowledge_base.title: Account repeatedly locks out during the day
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Account locked; repeated lockouts after unlocking; cannot sign in; lockout returns within minutes
knowledge_base.summary: Repeat lockouts are caused by a stale password cached somewhere, most often a phone mail profile or a mapped drive.
resolution_steps: Unlock the account and confirm the user can sign in on their primary device.
Ask the user whether their password was changed recently and on which devices they are signed in.
Sign out of corporate mail on the user's mobile device and sign back in with the current password.
Open Windows Credential Manager and remove stale corporate entries.
Disconnect and reconnect any mapped network drives using current credentials.
Monitor for a further lockout over the next two hours.
If lockouts continue, request a lockout source trace from the identity team.

knowledge_base.title: Multi-factor authentication device lost or replaced
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: New phone; MFA app not working; cannot approve sign-in; lost authenticator; no MFA prompt appears
knowledge_base.summary: A replaced phone leaves the old MFA registration in place. The registration must be reset through a verified identity check, never by email request alone.
resolution_steps: Verify the user's identity using the approved out-of-band process. Do not proceed on an email request alone.
Confirm with the user whether the old device is lost, stolen or simply replaced.
If the device is lost or stolen, raise a security note before resetting anything.
Reset the user's MFA registration in the identity portal.
Guide the user through enrolling the authenticator app on the new device.
Ask the user to complete a test sign-in and approve the prompt.
Confirm access to mail and VPN before closing the ticket.

knowledge_base.title: No audio or microphone in Teams meetings
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Cannot hear others in Teams; microphone not detected; headset not listed; audio works elsewhere but not in Teams
knowledge_base.summary: Teams keeps its own device selection separate from Windows. A headset working system-wide can still be unselected inside Teams.
resolution_steps: Confirm whether audio works outside Teams, for example in a media player.
Check the Windows sound settings and confirm the headset is the default device.
Open Teams device settings and select the headset for both speaker and microphone.
Run the Teams test call and confirm playback and recording.
If the headset is missing from the list, reconnect it and check the USB or Bluetooth connection.
Clear the Teams client cache if devices still do not appear.
If audio fails after a cache clear, reinstall the Teams client from the Company Software Center.

knowledge_base.title: Cannot send mail because mailbox is full
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Mailbox full warning; messages stuck in outbox; cannot send but can receive; quota exceeded message
knowledge_base.summary: Sending is blocked once the mailbox passes its quota. Clearing large items and the Deleted Items folder restores sending without a quota increase.
resolution_steps: Confirm the current mailbox size against the assigned quota.
Ask the user to empty Deleted Items and Junk Email.
Sort the mailbox by size and review the largest items with the user.
Move mail that must be kept into the user's online archive.
Confirm the mailbox is below quota and ask the user to retry sending.
If the outbox is still stuck, restart the mail client and retry.
If the user's role genuinely needs more space, raise a quota increase request for manager approval.

knowledge_base.title: Taskbar and File Explorer frozen but machine responds
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Taskbar not responding; Start menu will not open; File Explorer frozen; desktop icons unresponsive
knowledge_base.summary: A hung Windows Explorer shell freezes the desktop while the rest of the machine keeps running. Restarting the shell recovers it without a reboot.
resolution_steps: Confirm other applications still respond, which indicates a shell fault rather than a system hang.
Ask the user to save any open work before the shell is restarted.
Restart the Windows Explorer process. The taskbar and desktop disappear briefly.
Confirm the taskbar, Start menu and File Explorer are responsive again.
If the shell hangs again, check for pending Windows updates.
Review recently installed shell extensions or file-sync clients as a possible cause.
If the freeze repeats daily, escalate for a profile check.

knowledge_base.title: Windows updates repeatedly fail to install
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Update fails and rolls back; same update retries every day; error code during install; machine reports out of date
knowledge_base.summary: Repeated update failures are usually insufficient disk space or a damaged update cache rather than a faulty update.
resolution_steps: Record which update is failing and the reported error code.
Check free disk space and confirm at least 20 GB is available for the update.
Clear temporary files if space is short, then retry the update.
Run the Windows Update troubleshooter.
Check for pending updates again and allow the machine to retry during a maintenance window.
If the same update fails three times, capture the update log and escalate to the endpoint team.
Do not disable Windows Update as a workaround.

knowledge_base.title: External monitor not detected through dock or cable
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Second screen blank; monitor not detected; display not showing; extended desktop missing after docking
knowledge_base.summary: Undetected external displays are usually a cable or dock seating issue, or a graphics driver that failed to reload after docking.
resolution_steps: Confirm the monitor has power and the correct input source is selected.
Reseat the video cable at both the monitor and the dock.
Undock and redock the laptop, waiting ten seconds between.
Use the Windows display settings to detect displays manually.
Update the graphics and dock firmware from the Company Software Center.
Test the monitor with a different cable or a different port to isolate the fault.
If the monitor works on another machine but not this one, escalate for dock replacement.

knowledge_base.title: Laptop battery drains quickly or will not charge
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Battery drains in under two hours; not charging when plugged in; battery percentage jumps; charge stops below full
knowledge_base.summary: Fast drain is usually background load or an aged battery. A battery report distinguishes the two before any hardware is replaced.
resolution_steps: Confirm whether the laptop is charging through the dock or the supplied power adapter.
Generate a Windows battery report and compare design capacity with full charge capacity.
Check the top processes for background applications consuming CPU while idle.
Disable unnecessary startup applications that run in the background.
Update the power management and chipset drivers from the Company Software Center.
If full charge capacity is below 70 percent of design capacity, raise a battery replacement request.
If the battery does not charge at all with a known-good adapter, escalate as a hardware fault.

knowledge_base.title: Shared network drive not accessible
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Mapped drive shows red cross; access denied to share; cannot open department folder; drive letter missing
knowledge_base.summary: Disconnected shares are usually stale cached credentials or a VPN session that dropped, not a permissions change.
resolution_steps: Confirm the user is connected to the corporate network or VPN.
Test whether the share opens by its full network path.
Remove stale credentials for the file server from Windows Credential Manager.
Disconnect the mapped drive and reconnect it using current credentials.
If access is denied rather than unavailable, confirm the user's group membership with the data owner.
Confirm the user can open and save a test file.
If permissions are genuinely missing, route the access request to the data owner for approval.

knowledge_base.title: Application crashes immediately after an update
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: App closes on launch; crash on startup after update; application stopped working; worked yesterday
knowledge_base.summary: Post-update crashes are commonly a corrupt local profile or cache rather than a faulty package. Clear local state before reinstalling.
resolution_steps: Record the application name, version and the exact time the crash started.
Check Windows Event Viewer for the application error entry.
Confirm whether other users on the same version are affected, to separate a local fault from a bad release.
Clear the application's local cache or reset its user profile.
Relaunch and confirm whether the crash persists.
If it persists, reinstall the application from the Company Software Center.
If several users on the same version are affected, escalate as a release issue and do not reinstall further machines.

knowledge_base.title: File transfers to the network share are very slow
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Copying files takes far too long; transfer speed drops; slow save to shared drive; timeouts copying large files
knowledge_base.summary: Slow transfers are usually Wi-Fi contention, VPN routing or an antivirus on-access scan, not a fault on the file server.
resolution_steps: Record the transfer speed and the file size used for the test.
Test the same transfer on a wired connection to rule out Wi-Fi contention.
Confirm whether the user is on VPN and whether the share is reachable without it.
Check whether an antivirus scan is running and consuming CPU during the transfer.
Test connectivity and latency to the file server.
Retry the transfer outside the scheduled scan window and compare speeds.
If the wired transfer is also slow for all users, escalate to the storage team.

knowledge_base.title: User reports a suspected phishing email
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Suspicious email; asked for password by email; unexpected invoice link; sender looks wrong; clicked a bad link
knowledge_base.summary: Phishing reports are handled by the security team. Support's role is to preserve evidence and contain the account, never to test the link.
resolution_steps: Do not open links or attachments in the reported message under any circumstances.
Ask the user whether they clicked a link, opened an attachment or entered credentials.
If credentials were entered, reset the user's password immediately and revoke active sessions.
Report the message through the approved phishing reporting button so headers are preserved.
Leave the original message in place until the security team confirms it can be removed.
Raise a security incident ticket and assign it to the security team.
Do not close the ticket until the security team confirms the outcome.

knowledge_base.title: Browser homepage changed and unknown extension installed
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Homepage changed by itself; unknown toolbar; search redirects; pop-up adverts; extension the user did not install
knowledge_base.summary: An unrequested extension or changed search provider is treated as a potential compromise, not a preference change.
resolution_steps: Record the extension name and the changed homepage or search provider before anything is removed.
Ask the user what they installed or downloaded recently.
Disable the unknown extension rather than deleting it, so it can be examined.
Reset the browser homepage and search provider to the corporate default.
Run a full endpoint antivirus scan and record the result.
If the scan finds anything, raise a security incident and hand over to the security team.
Confirm with the user that redirects and pop-ups have stopped before closing.

knowledge_base.title: Bluetooth headset or mouse will not pair
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Bluetooth device not pairing; headset not connecting; mouse drops connection; device not found in Bluetooth list
knowledge_base.summary: Pairing failures are usually a device still bonded to another machine, or a Bluetooth stack that needs restarting.
resolution_steps: Confirm the device is charged and in pairing mode.
Check whether the device is still connected to the user's phone or another laptop and disconnect it there.
Remove the existing pairing entry from Windows Bluetooth settings.
Toggle Bluetooth off and on, then pair the device again.
Update Bluetooth drivers from the Company Software Center if pairing still fails.
Test the device on another machine to confirm whether the fault is the device or the laptop.
If the device fails on two machines, raise a peripheral replacement request.

knowledge_base.title: VPN connects but internal applications are unreachable
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: VPN shows connected but nothing loads; internal apps time out on VPN; routes missing; works in office but not remote
knowledge_base.summary: A connected VPN with no internal access is normally a routing or split-tunnel problem rather than an authentication failure.
resolution_steps: Confirm the VPN client reports connected and note the assigned IP address.
Test connectivity to an internal host by IP and then by hostname.
Flush the DNS resolver cache and retest by hostname.
Disconnect and reconnect the VPN so routes are reapplied.
Confirm the correct VPN profile is selected, as a split-tunnel profile may exclude internal ranges.
Reimport the current VPN configuration from the IT portal if the profile is outdated.
If routes are still missing after reconnect, escalate to the network team with the IP and route details.

knowledge_base.title: Password expired while working remotely
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Password expired; cannot change password off network; locked out remotely; sign-in says password must change
knowledge_base.summary: An expired password cannot always be changed off the corporate network. The user must first establish a VPN session that permits a password change.
resolution_steps: Verify the user's identity using the approved out-of-band process.
Ask the user to connect the VPN using the pre-login or credential-provider option if available.
Guide the user to change the password through the standard Windows change-password screen while connected.
If the VPN cannot connect, reset the password through the identity portal after identity verification.
Ask the user to lock and unlock the workstation so the new password is cached locally.
Remove stale credentials from Windows Credential Manager.
Confirm the user can access mail, VPN and one internal site before closing.

knowledge_base.title: Disk health warning reported on user laptop
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: SMART warning; disk error reported; Windows says back up your files; clicking noise; unexpected freezes
knowledge_base.summary: A disk health warning is treated as imminent failure. Protecting the user's data comes before any diagnostic or repair step.
resolution_steps: Record the exact warning text and the drive model.
Confirm the user's files are backed up to OneDrive or the approved backup location before anything else.
Do not run extended disk repair tools on a failing drive, as this can accelerate data loss.
Check free disk space and system health, and capture the results for the hardware ticket.
Arrange a replacement device or drive with the hardware team.
Transfer the user's profile and data to the replacement once backup is verified.
Return the failed drive through the approved secure disposal process.

knowledge_base.title: Antivirus scan makes the machine unusable during work hours
knowledge_base.issue_pattern: Machine very slow at the same time daily; antivirus using high CPU; fans loud mid-morning; slow while scanning
knowledge_base.summary: Scheduled scans running during working hours cause predictable slowdowns. The schedule is changed centrally, never by disabling protection.
resolution_steps: Confirm the slowdown happens at a consistent time each day.
List the top processes during the slowdown and confirm the antivirus service is the main consumer.
Check the configured scan schedule on the endpoint.
Do not disable or pause antivirus protection as a workaround.
Request a scan-schedule change to outside the user's working hours through the endpoint team.
Confirm with the user over the following two days that the slowdown no longer occurs during work.
If the machine is slow outside scan windows too, investigate performance separately.
